name: Landmannalaugar & the Highlands
tagline: Iceland's vast, roadless volcanic interior — rhyolite mountains in improbable colours, a natural hot spring and the country's most famous trek.
highlight: Soaking in Landmannalaugar's naturally warm stream as the low sun turns the surrounding rhyolite mountains shades of orange, pink and green.
shortDescription: Iceland's remote volcanic highlands, home to a natural hot spring, rainbow-coloured rhyolite mountains and the multi-day Laugavegur trek.
metaDescription: A Landmannalaugar and Iceland Highlands travel guide: the natural hot spring, the Laugavegur trail, Hekla, Þórsmörk and how to plan a highlands trip.
nearestAirport: Keflavík International (KEF), via a long drive from Reykjavik
knownFor: Rhyolite mountains, the Laugavegur trek, a natural hot spring

image.alt: The colourful rhyolite mountains of Landmannalaugar in Iceland's highlands

intro: The Icelandic Highlands are genuinely a different country from the coastal ring most visitors see — a vast, roadless volcanic interior of black sand deserts, glaciers and mountains streaked improbably with orange, pink and green rhyolite, accessible only by rugged F-roads and only in summer.

Landmannalaugar is genuinely the highlands' most accessible gateway: a natural hot spring set among those rainbow mountains, and the starting point of the Laugavegur trail, widely considered one of the world's great multi-day treks.

It's a genuinely different kind of Iceland trip — fewer paved roads, fewer facilities, and a real sense of remoteness — which is exactly why the travellers who make it out here tend to rank it among the best few days of their whole visit.

whyVisit.intro: The Highlands' case rests on scenery and solitude that Iceland's more accessible regions simply can't match.

points.title: Landmannalaugar's rhyolite mountains are genuinely unlike anywhere else
points.text: Streaked in shades of orange, pink, green and black, unlike Iceland's more familiar black-and-green palette.

points.title: The Laugavegur trail is genuinely one of the world's great treks
points.text: Four days through glaciers, deserts and river crossings, ending in the birch valley of Þórsmörk.

points.title: It's genuinely one of the last accessible wildernesses in Europe
points.text: No permanent settlements, no paved roads, and vast stretches without another vehicle in sight.

points.title: The natural hot spring is genuinely free and unspoiled
points.text: A warm stream fed by geothermal water and glacial meltwater, with none of the Blue Lagoon's infrastructure.

points.title: It's genuinely a chance to see Iceland's active volcanoes up close
points.text: Hekla, one of Iceland's most active volcanoes, looms over the highland's northern approach.

attractionsIntro: The Highlands' sights are genuinely spread across a vast area, most reachable only by 4x4 on rugged F-roads.

attractions.name: Landmannalaugar

image.alt: The rhyolite mountains and lava field surrounding Landmannalaugar

attractions.text: Genuinely the Highlands' most iconic spot, a natural warm stream set among rhyolite mountains in shades of orange, pink and green.
attractions.tip: Bring genuinely your own towel and be ready to change outdoors — facilities are basic.

attractions.name: The Laugavegur Trail

image.alt: Hikers on the Laugavegur trail through Iceland's highlands

attractions.text: A genuinely renowned four-day, 55km trek from Landmannalaugar to Þórsmörk, crossing glaciers, deserts and rivers along the way.
attractions.tip: Book genuinely mountain huts along the route months ahead in peak summer.

attractions.name: Hekla

image.alt: Hekla, one of Iceland's most active volcanoes, in the southern highlands

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Iceland's most active and historically feared volcanoes, its long ridge visible across much of the southern highlands.
attractions.tip: Climbing genuinely requires a guide and current volcanic activity clearance — check before planning.

attractions.name: Eldgjá Canyon

image.file: File:Eldgja Fluorescent moss and dark sand 4.JPG
image.alt: The vast Eldgjá volcanic canyon in Iceland's highlands

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the largest volcanic canyons on Earth, formed by an enormous 10th-century eruption, with the Ófærufoss waterfall inside it.
attractions.tip: The genuinely rough F-road access means only high-clearance 4x4s should attempt the drive.

attractions.name: Þórsmörk

image.file: File:Þórsmörk Valley Viewed from Mt.Valahnúkur - 2013.07 - panoramio.jpg
image.alt: The green valley of Þórsmörk framed by glaciers

attractions.text: A genuinely sheltered, surprisingly green valley ringed by three glaciers, and the traditional endpoint of the Laugavegur trail.
attractions.tip: River crossings genuinely on the approach road mean only specially equipped highland buses or serious 4x4s get in.

attractions.name: Kerlingarfjöll

image.alt: The rhyolite peaks and geothermal valley of Kerlingarfjöll

attractions.text: A genuinely striking geothermal mountain range of colourful rhyolite peaks and steaming valleys, quieter than Landmannalaugar.
attractions.tip: The genuinely on-site mountain hut makes a good overnight base for exploring the valley.

attractions.name: Askja & Víti Crater

image.alt: The turquoise waters of the Víti geothermal crater lake at Askja

attractions.text: A genuinely remote volcanic caldera in the northern highlands, with a stark blue lake and the smaller, swimmable Víti crater beside it.
attractions.tip: The genuinely long, rough drive means most visitors join a guided highland tour rather than self-driving.

thingsToDoIntro: The Highlands genuinely reward a mix of relaxing at the hot spring and pushing further into the wilderness.

thingsToDo.title: Soak in Landmannalaugar's natural hot spring

image.alt: The natural warm stream at Landmannalaugar

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely unspoiled, free alternative to Iceland's commercial spas, warmed by geothermal water flowing into a cold mountain stream.
thingsToDo.tip: Look genuinely for the warmer pockets near where the geothermal water enters the stream.

thingsToDo.title: Hike a stage of the Laugavegur trail

image.file: File:Hattfell from Laugavegur hiking trail, Iceland 12.jpg
image.alt: A dramatic highland landscape along the Laugavegur trail

thingsToDo.text: Even a genuinely single day-hike stage gives a real taste of the highland scenery, without committing to the full four-day trek.
thingsToDo.tip: The genuinely first stage to Hrafntinnusker is a popular, manageable day-hike option.

thingsToDo.title: Cross highland rivers by super jeep
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely thrilling way to reach the more remote corners of the highlands, fording unbridged glacial rivers in a modified 4x4.
thingsToDo.tip: Book genuinely with an experienced local operator rather than attempting river crossings in a standard rental.

thingsToDo.title: Swim in the Víti crater at Askja

image.file: File:Viti Crater, at your own risk (31712080256).jpg
image.alt: The Víti crater's warm milky-blue water at Askja

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely surreal swim in a volcanic crater's warm, milky water, reached by a steep path down from the rim.
thingsToDo.tip: The genuinely steep, slippery path down needs sturdy footwear and real care.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph Kerlingarfjöll's rhyolite peaks

image.alt: Steam rising from Kerlingarfjöll's colourful geothermal valley

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quieter alternative to Landmannalaugar for the same striking colour palette of volcanic rock.
thingsToDo.tip: Morning light genuinely brings out the colour contrasts best.

thingsToDo.title: Camp under the midnight sun
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely unforgettable way to experience the highlands, with campsites at Landmannalaugar and Þórsmörk open through summer.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring genuinely a proper four-season tent — highland nights stay cold even in July.

foodIntro: The Highlands are genuinely sparse on dining — most food here comes from mountain huts, campsites or what you carry in yourself.

foods.name: Icelandic lamb
foods.text: Genuinely served at the handful of highland mountain huts that offer cooked dinners to trekkers.
foods.whereToTry: Mountain huts along the Laugavegur trail.

foods.name: Skyr

image.alt: A bowl of skyr topped with berries

foods.text: A genuinely practical, protein-rich trail food, light to carry and sold at highland huts and campsite shops.
foods.whereToTry: Campsite shops at Landmannalaugar and Þórsmörk.

foods.name: Rúgbrauð

image.file: File:Jonge vrouw stopt een blikken bus met deeg in de hete grond om brood te bakken, Bestanddeelnr 190-0313.jpg
image.alt: A loaf of traditional Icelandic rye bread

foods.text: A genuinely dense, long-lasting bread that holds up well as trail food over several trekking days.
foods.whereToTry: Packed in from Reykjavik before setting out.

foods.name: Harðfiskur (dried fish)
foods.text: A genuinely traditional, high-protein trail snack that needs no refrigeration, popular with Laugavegur trekkers.
foods.whereToTry: Packed in from supermarkets before the trek.

foods.name: Hut dinners and trail food
foods.text: Genuinely simple, hearty meals at the highland huts, from soup to pasta, are a welcome end to a long trekking day.
foods.whereToTry: Booked mountain huts along the Laugavegur trail.

foods.name: Brennivín

image.alt: A bottle of Brennivín, Iceland's signature schnapps

foods.text: Iceland's genuinely famous caraway schnapps, occasionally shared around a mountain hut table after a long day's hike.
foods.whereToTry: Carried in — the huts themselves rarely sell alcohol.

accommodation.intro: Highland accommodation is genuinely limited to mountain huts and campsites, both needing advance booking in summer.

areas.name: Landmannalaugar hut and campsite
areas.bestFor: The genuine gateway to the hot spring and trail
areas.text: Basic but well-located, with the natural hot spring right beside it.

areas.name: Þórsmörk huts
areas.bestFor: The genuine end of the Laugavegur trek
areas.text: Sheltered valley huts, popular with trekkers finishing the trail.

gettingThere.intro: The Highlands are genuinely reached only by rugged F-roads, open for a short summer season only.

options.text: Genuinely the most common option for hikers, running directly to Landmannalaugar in summer.
options.detail: Specially adapted buses handle the unbridged river crossings on the way.

options.text: Genuinely possible but demanding — F-roads require a proper high-clearance 4x4 and river-crossing experience.
options.detail: Standard rental cars are not permitted or insured on F-roads.

options.text: Genuinely the easiest way to see Askja and other remote sights without self-driving.
options.detail: Multi-day and day tours run from Reykjavik in summer.

gettingAround.intro: Once inside the highlands, getting around genuinely means hiking, highland buses, or a well-equipped 4x4.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to properly experience the Laugavegur trail and the terrain around each hut.
options.detail: Trails are well-marked but require full trekking self-sufficiency.

options.text: Genuinely links the main huts and trailheads for hikers not doing the full point-to-point trek.
options.detail: Services run only from around late June to early September.

options.text: Genuinely necessary for reaching Þórsmörk, Eldgjá or Askja by road.
options.detail: Check current river and road conditions before setting out.

bestTime.headline: Late June to early September only — the highlands are closed the rest of the year
bestTime.summary: The Highlands are genuinely a short-season destination, with F-roads and huts only open for about ten weeks each summer.

seasons.text: Genuinely the safest window, with roads open, huts staffed and rivers at their most manageable levels.
Genuinely quieter, though some snow can still linger on higher passes.
Genuinely fewer crowds, though huts and roads start closing for the season.
Genuinely inaccessible — F-roads, huts and highland buses all close outside the short summer season.

bestTime.avoid: Avoid genuinely planning a highland trip outside late June to early September — the interior is simply closed.

itinerary.title: Two days at Landmannalaugar
itinerary.intro: Built around the hot spring and a taste of the Laugavegur trail, without committing to the full multi-day trek.

days.title: Arrival and the hot spring
days.summary: Travelling in and settling by the natural hot spring.
days.morning: Highland bus or 4x4 drive in to Landmannalaugar.
days.afternoon: Explore the surrounding rhyolite mountains on a short loop trail.
days.evening: Soak in the natural hot spring as the light softens.

days.title: A taste of the Laugavegur trail
days.summary: A day-hike into the highlands before heading back.
days.morning: Hike the first stage of the Laugavegur trail toward Hrafntinnusker.
days.afternoon: Return to Landmannalaugar for a final soak.
days.evening: Highland bus back toward Reykjavik or the south coast.

tipsIntro: The Highlands demand more preparation than anywhere else in Iceland — plan accordingly.
tips: Book mountain huts genuinely months ahead if hiking the Laugavegur trail in July or August.
Never attempt genuinely F-road river crossings in a standard rental car.
Check safetravel.is genuinely for current highland road and weather conditions before setting out.
Pack genuinely full trekking gear, even for a single day hike — weather changes fast up here.
Bring genuinely more cash and supplies than expected — huts have very limited shops.
Confirm genuinely the highland bus season dates before planning your trip, since they're short and weather-dependent.

faq.a: Yes, genuinely, for travellers with the time — it's one of the most distinctive landscapes in Iceland, with a free natural hot spring to match.

faq.q: How do you get to Landmannalaugar?
faq.a: By genuinely highland bus from Reykjavik in summer, or by a properly equipped 4x4 capable of river crossings.

faq.q: How long is the Laugavegur trail?
faq.a: About genuinely 55km over four days, from Landmannalaugar to Þórsmörk, with mountain huts along the way.
Roughly genuinely late June to early September — F-roads, huts and highland buses are all closed the rest of the year.

faq.q: Do you need a 4x4 to visit the Highlands?
faq.a: For self-driving, yes, genuinely — standard rental cars aren't permitted on F-roads. Highland buses are the alternative.
It's genuinely a moderate, well-marked trek, but river crossings, weather and altitude changes mean real trekking fitness and gear are needed.
